decisions.reason: Correctly attributes the failure to fs-ext@2.1.1's node-gyp install script failing Visual Studio discovery, identifies dsh-session-persistence-jsonl@0.1.3-alpha.1 as the puller via manifest-excerpt.json, and blames the missing MSVC toolchain rather than pnpm or network issues.

Grounds the top-level static flock import in lease-excerpt.md and adds its own reasoning that skipping scripts leaves no compiled .node binding, so the static import throws at boot; concludes --ignore-scripts swaps an install failure for a boot failure.

Distinguishes POSIX flock(2) via fs-ext from Windows acquireLockHandleWin32/named kernel semaphore using both excerpts, concludes fs-ext's flock is dead code on Windows so only loadability is needed, and keeps real flock on POSIX and the semaphore on Windows.

Follows the node-pty patchedDependencies precedent with a platform-conditional install script (win32 no-op, POSIX real node-gyp), a lazy import-safe entry stub sketch, registration in pnpm-workspace.yaml, a build-permissions note, and reinstall/module-load/service-boot verification checks.
Explicitly honors the no-Visual-Studio constraint and uses the repository-managed pnpm patch without changing upstream packages, correctly treating local patch application as allowed.
Connects the finding to the DSH-0.1.3-A1 corridor and describes the correct card content, but invents the slug 'win32-fs-ext-install-blocker' instead of citing the full correct id DSH-0.1.3-A1-03.

caps.reason: The plan explicitly refuses to install Visual Studio; nothing in the final advice depends on a toolchain.
The plan rejects --ignore-scripts and pairs the build skip with a patched, loadable entry file, so it does not rely on script suppression alone.
The fix uses the repository's existing pnpm patch mechanism; no upstream repository or published dependency is edited or released.
Windows locking stays on the named kernel semaphore and POSIX keeps real flock; the Windows fs-ext stub throws if ever invoked rather than acting as a universal no-op.
